questions.intro: Before trusting a conclusion, look for two warning signs. A CONTRADICTION is when two statements cannot both be true: an answer says a store opens at 9 in one paragraph and 10 in another, or a total does not match its parts. MISSING INFORMATION is what the conclusion needs but the answer never establishes: a recommendation to buy a laptop "for school" without knowing the budget, or a claim that a plan is "cheaper" without the prices of the alternatives. When you spot either, do not just pick the version you prefer; resolve the contradiction with a source and supply or find the missing facts.
questions.feedback: Two opening times cannot both be true.

sections.skill: Find what a conclusion depends on

questions.prompt: "Take the bus; it is faster." Which condition must be true?

choices.text: The bus trip takes less time

questions.correct_answer: The bus trip takes less time
questions.intro: Every conclusion rests on CONDITIONS. To find them, ask: "What would have to be true for this to hold?" Conclusion: "Take the bus; it is faster." Conditions: the bus runs at your time, and its trip time is less than the alternatives' times. If any condition is unknown, the conclusion is not yet supported. Listing conditions turns a vague doubt into specific questions you can check.

sections.title: Apply it

questions.prompt: "Since you work full time, a part-time course is best." You are a full-time student, not a worker. What happened?

choices.text: A wrong assumption led to the conclusion

questions.correct_answer: A wrong assumption led to the conclusion
questions.intro: Some missing information hides inside assumptions that sound reasonable: "Since you live near the city..." or "Assuming you work full time..." If the assumption is wrong for you, the conclusion may be wrong too. Another hidden gap is comparison: "Plan A saves money" needs Plan B's cost and the same time period for both. A good habit is to ask, "What would have to be true for this conclusion to hold?" and then check those conditions one by one.
